1. Production SRE Methodology Upgrade (Closed-Model vs. Open-Model)

To eliminate synthetic benchmark blind spots, we upgraded our stress-testing harness from a basic 3-endpoint empty-DB loop to a full 3-stage Production SRE qualification suite.

Dimension Initial Closed-Model Baseline Upgraded Production SRE Suite Engineering Impact
Database State 0 Chat Sessions, 0 Messages (items: [], 2 bytes) 1,500 Sessions & 15,000 Messages (15 sessions/user × 10 msgs w/ citations & chunks) Exercises real B-Tree index scans, cursor pagination (SESSION_PAGE_SIZE = 10), and ~4.6 KB JSON serialization.
Endpoint Coverage 3 Endpoints (GET /auth/me, GET /chat-sessions, PATCH /auth/me) 6-Endpoint Production Mix (+ Page 2 Cursor, Regex ?q=Transformer, GET /chat-sessions/:id, PATCH /chat-sessions/:id) Disclosed that GET /chat-sessions/:id (30% of traffic) executes 2 sequential WAN round-trips, doubling its latency floor.
Workload Generator Closed Model (ramping-vus with sleep(0.5–1.5s)) Open Model (ramping-arrival-rate) + Strict 2.0s Client Timeout Eliminates Coordinated Omission; measures true arrival queuing and timeout cliffs when the DB tunnel saturates.
Auth Crypto & Telemetry Pre-signed JWTs only; client-side k6 metrics only Stage C Argon2id Login + Refresh Rotation + 2s Server CPU/RAM Telemetry Proves CRUD is WAN I/O-bound (30.1% CPU) while Argon2id saturates libuv threads (310.2% CPU) without blocking the Event Loop.
Infrastructure Topology Discovery (Cloudflare TCP Tunnel): Inspecting active TCP sockets revealed that localhost:27017 is served by cloudflared.exe access tcp --hostname mongodb.minio-quangmanh.io.vn (PID 26132). Every MongoDB command traverses a WAN tunnel with a physical RTT floor of 112–118 ms. Consequently, single-query endpoints have a physical floor of ~115 ms, while 2-query sequential endpoints (GET /api/v1/chat-sessions/:id) have a physical floor of ~235–265 ms.

3. Stage B: Rule L1 3-Minute Hold-Out & 6-Endpoint Latency Breakdown

Per Rule L1, we executed continuous 3-minute (180s) Open-Model hold-out runs (k6_prod_certified_holdout.ts) at 65 RPS (12,812 requests, 59 MB received) and 50 RPS (9,924 requests, 46 MB received) representing 100 Concurrent Users (100 CUs).

Endpoint in Traffic Mix Traffic Share DB Operations per Request Min Latency P50 (Median) Mean (Avg) P90 Latency P95 Latency Check Pass Rate
GET /api/v1/auth/me 15% 1× users.findById 113.54 ms 174.56 ms 293.29 ms 558.43 ms 581.03 ms 100.00% ✓
PATCH /api/v1/auth/me 5% 1× users.findByIdAndUpdate 114.19 ms 180.10 ms 304.10 ms 556.85 ms 576.57 ms 100.00% ✓
PATCH /api/v1/chat-sessions/:id 10% 1× chat_sessions.findOneAndUpdate 116.18 ms 180.40 ms 305.08 ms 559.11 ms 587.17 ms 100.00% ✓
GET /api/v1/chat-sessions?cursor|q 10% 1× Index Range / Regex Scan (Page 2) 113.51 ms 188.32 ms 307.72 ms 566.02 ms 586.93 ms 100.00% ✓
GET /api/v1/chat-sessions 30% 1× Index Scan (Page 1, 10 items + cursor) 113.40 ms 188.57 ms 306.38 ms 564.97 ms 595.96 ms 100.00% ✓
GET /api/v1/chat-sessions/:id 30% 2× Sequential Queries (findOwned + messages.find) 236.51 ms 408.09 ms (2.1×) 634.74 ms (2.1×) 1,160.00 ms (2.1×) 1,210.00 ms (2.0×) 100.00% ✓
Root-Cause Finding — The 2.0× Sequential Query Signature: Every percentile of GET /api/v1/chat-sessions/:id (min = 236.5ms, P50 = 408.1ms, avg = 634.7ms, P95 = 1,210ms) is literally 2.05× the latency of the 5 single-query endpoints (min = 113.5ms, P50 = 188.6ms, avg = 306.4ms, P95 = 587.2ms). In ChatSessionsService.get() (src/chat-sessions/chat-sessions.service.ts:172-179), await this.findOwned(id, userId) executes first, and only after that WAN round-trip completes does await this.messages.find({ session_id: s._id }) begin. Running both queries concurrently via Promise.all will immediately halve GET /api/v1/chat-sessions/:id latency (~200ms P50, ~580ms P95).
Figure 2: Per-endpoint latency breakdown during the 3-minute hold-out (12,812 requests, 0.00% error rate), illustrating the 2.0× sequential WAN query cost on GET /sessions/:id.

Using collect_telemetry.js (sampling every 2s) and k6_prod_auth_crypto.ts (ramping up to 50 concurrent POST /api/v1/auth/login Argon2id verifications + POST /api/v1/auth/refresh rotations + GET /api/v1/auth/me Event Loop probes), we measured server-side hardware utilization and threadpool isolation.

Stage / Metric Process CPU % (1-Core Equiv) Working Set RAM (MB) Latency / Pass Rate Architectural Diagnosis
Stage B: 3-Min Session Hold-Out node.exe (PID 12076) Min: 15.6% · Avg: 30.1% · Max: 64.0% Min: 1,980.7 · Avg: 2,062.0 · Max: 2,108.6 12,812 / 12,812 (100.00% OK) Purely WAN I/O-Bound; V8 Event Loop is 70% idle; zero memory leak over 3m25s.
Stage B: Cloudflare DB Tunnel cloudflared.exe (PID 26132) Min: 0.8% · Avg: 3.9% · Max: 8.9% Min: 35.8 · Avg: 44.8 · Max: 45.9 286 kB/s Rx · 25 kB/s Tx Stable tunnel multiplexing; bounded by WAN RTT (~115ms) rather than local CPU.
Stage C: Argon2id Login Flood (2→50 VUs) node.exe (PID 12076) Avg: 203.9% · Max: 310.2% (~3.1 Cores) Avg: 2,210.3 · Max: 2,352.4 → 2,100.4 P50: 2.73s · 100% OK @ ≤25 VUs (93.5% @ 50 VUs) libuv Threadpool-Bound (UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE=4) + 4 sequential MongoDB queries/login.
Stage C: Refresh Token Rotation POST /api/v1/auth/refresh Shared w/ Login Flood Shared w/ Login Flood Min: 501.4ms · P50: 707.2ms · 100.00% (302/302) Atomic single-use consume + family rotation verified with 0 race errors.
Stage C: Event Loop Responsiveness Probe GET /api/v1/auth/me Main JS Thread Main JS Thread Min: 119.4ms · P50: 177.7ms · P95: 566.1ms (100% OK) Main JS Event Loop Unblocked! Argon2id offloads cleanly to C++ worker threads.
